thinkers.name: Hans Urs von Balthasar
thinkers.tradition: Theologian of glory, drama, and time; Ratzinger's closest ally
thinkers.claim: In Jesus eternity enters time: the Son who has time for God is where God has time for the world.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: eternity is not timelessness but dominion over time, the creatively supporting power of the present in every age.
thinkers.quote: Son, who has time, in the world, for God, is the point at which God has time for the world.

thinkers.name: Henri de Lubac
thinkers.tradition: Jesuit theologian; the Church's holiness and atheistic humanism's drama
thinkers.claim: The Church is holy not because her members are holy but because the Lord bestows holiness on her unmerited.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: holiness is not separation but union; Christ drew sin to himself, so the Church bears the lost within her.
thinkers.quote: a “holy Church” that is holy because the Lord bestows holiness on her as a quite unmerited gift

thinkers.name: Romano Guardini
thinkers.tradition: Catholic theologian of revelation; discernment of what is Christian
thinkers.claim: True humility lets God do what seems to us unfitting — to bow down in Christ — rather than contriving God for ourselves.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: bracketing Christ's divinity gains nothing; the fear that it alienates him hides distrust of God's astonishing nearness.
thinkers.quote: the higher form of humility consists in allowing God to do precisely what appears to us to be unfitting

thinkers.name: Augustine of Hippo
thinkers.tradition: Bishop of Hippo; Trinity as relation, faith seeking understanding
thinkers.claim: God is substance and relation: Father is relation to Son; person is pure relation, the exchange of word and love.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: relation is an equally valid primordial mode of reality; yet the early Augustine's “God and the soul” program is unchristian.
thinkers.quote: In God there are no accidents, only substance and relation.

thinkers.name: Anselm of Canterbury
thinkers.tradition: Medieval theologian; satisfaction theory of atonement, Cur Deus homo
thinkers.claim: Sin infinitely offends God; only the God-man can make infinite satisfaction, restoring by necessary reasons the violated order of justice.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: Anselm's rigid legal logic distorts perspectives and darkens God; the Cross is Christ's self-giving, not a payment God demands.
thinkers.quote: the perfectly logical divine-cum-human legal system erected by Anselm distorts the perspectives

thinkers.name: Irenaeus of Lyon
thinkers.tradition: Early Church Father; Christ recapitulates humanity, restoring fallen Adam
thinkers.claim: Christ recapitulates humanity's whole history, gathering the creature “Adam” in himself and restoring in himself what the first Adam lost.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: the gathering takes the form of the Cross; the “body of Christ” must draw to itself the whole of mankind.
thinkers.quote: So if Jesus is called “Adam”, this implies that he is intended to gather the whole creature “Adam” in himself.

thinkers.name: Rudolf Bultmann
thinkers.tradition: New Testament scholar; kerygma theology and demythologizing
thinkers.claim: Only Jesus' bare existence matters; faith rests not on uncertain historical hypotheses but on the preached word that opens closed existence.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: an empty event is no easier to swallow than one filled with content; who Jesus is cannot be bypassed.
thinkers.quote: But is an empty event any easier to swallow than one filled with content?

thinkers.name: Karl Rahner
thinkers.tradition: Jesuit theologian; Ratzinger's great creditor, but he resists transcendental method
thinkers.claim: The transcendental method grounds faith in the subject's self-experience, where God is already encountered as the horizon within.
thinkers.counter: With Baader and Möhler, Ratzinger: knowledge of God, like love, is never deduced from self-awareness but always comes “from another”.
thinkers.quote: human knowledge is only reality when it is being known, being brought to knowledge, and thus again “from another”

thinkers.name: Ludwig Feuerbach
thinkers.tradition: Philosopher of religion; God as man's projected essence
thinkers.claim: Religion is a wish-dream: man projects his own essence as God; maturity means shaking off the dream and facing reality.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: faith is no wish-fulfillment — Christianity's God comes so near that we can kill him and absents himself on Holy Saturday.
thinkers.quote: Have we not a duty to break with the dream and to face reality?

thinkers.name: Karl Marx
thinkers.tradition: Philosopher of praxis; change the world rather than interpret it
thinkers.claim: Philosophy must stop interpreting the world and change it; truth lies in the makable future, not in received being.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: the Credo is not a program for changing the world; belief lives on neither the plane of fact nor makability.
thinkers.quote: So far philosophers have merely interpreted the world in various ways; it is necessary to change it.

thinkers.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
thinkers.tradition: Philosopher; death of God, the last man, revaluation of values
thinkers.claim: God is dead and we have killed him; the Christian God is overcome and man must become more than mere man.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: Nietzsche's cry is Holy Saturday, already confessed in the Creed; the image of God we formed had to die.
thinkers.quote: Holy Saturday is the day of the “death of God”, the day that expresses the unparalleled experience of our age

thinkers.name: G. W. F. Hegel
thinkers.tradition: Idealist philosopher; God realized in the historical process
thinkers.claim: Read speculatively, the Trinity is the key to being: God comes to himself only in history's dialectical process.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: total logic dissolves into myth — a God born historically — and turns political: the apotheosis of the state.
thinkers.quote: The attempt at total logic ends in illogicality, in the self-dissolution of logic into myth.

thinkers.name: Ernst Bloch
thinkers.tradition: Marxist philosopher of hope and utopia
thinkers.claim: Hope is praxis toward the future we make: the suffering proletariat redeems the world through class struggle, not grace.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger: man comes to himself not through what he does but what he accepts; the Cross is a suffering-for, not struggle-against.
thinkers.quote: Here lies possibly the deepest division between the Christian principle of hope and its Marxist modification.

thinkers.name: Martin Heidegger
thinkers.tradition: Phenomenologist of thinking and being; calculative versus reflective thought
thinkers.claim: Calculating thought and reflective thought are both legitimate and irreducible; today calculation's triumphs threaten man with thoughtlessness.
thinkers.counter: Ratzinger completes the pair: reflective thought needs a ground to stand on — the logos; understanding grows only out of belief.
thinkers.quote: calculating thought, which is concerned with “makability”, and reflective thought, which is concerned with meaning
